findings.title: Reset has no durable boundary against pre-reset snapshots
findings.problem: resetAll deletes the progress row and restarts its revision, but saves carry no reset generation. A different revision-aware tab can subsequently refetch the reset row and reconcile its pre-reset history back into it. The legacy_hold protection also disappears on the first successful update because writeAt always sets legacy_hold to false.
findings.failure_scenario: Open the account on two devices. Reset progress on device A, then answer a question there. Device B still holds the old history; its next save conflicts, refetches A's row, and reconcileProgress unions the old history back in. Likewise, an old-client snapshot arriving after A's first update is parked and restored on a later load. Answers that the student explicitly erased reappear.
findings.fix: Persist a reset generation or tombstone that survives ordinary saves. Reject or explicitly rebase snapshots from an earlier generation instead of unioning their baseline history into the reset account. Test both revision-aware and legacy writers after a post-reset answer has already saved.

findings.title: Reconciliation loses covers earned and consumed between acknowledgements
findings.problem: replayUnseen and replayActivity replay study days using only the baseline's covers; neither replays cover grants. reconcileProgress then adds newly recorded coverWeeks grants after replaying the streak. A cover earned and spent after the baseline is therefore unavailable when the gap is evaluated, and is subsequently returned as an unspent cover.
findings.failure_scenario: Start with shield=false and covers=0. While saves are failing, study eight questions Monday through Friday, earn a cover, miss Saturday, and study Sunday using that cover. When saving resumes against the earlier accepted baseline, reconciliation restarts the streak on Sunday and restores one banked cover instead of preserving the protected streak and zero remaining covers. This happens even without another device changing the server.
findings.fix: Reconcile cover grants and consumption in chronological order with study activity, or preserve the local activity result when only the local side changed. Add a regression covering an earned-and-spent cover across an unacknowledged baseline, asserting both streak and remaining covers.

findings.title: Legacy matching silently discards distinct answers with colliding IDs
findings.problem: sameLegacyOccurrence matches undated, attempt-less rows without comparing category or canonical identity. pendingRowKey makes the same omission. Consequently, foldPendingProgress can mistake a different question's answer for an already stored occurrence and discard it.
findings.failure_scenario: The stored log contains an attempt-less builtin:7 answer in Management of Care. A parked old-client snapshot from another device contains an independent numeric question 7 answer in Pharmacology with the same correct boolean and no timestamps. mergeLogs matches the two rows despite their different categories; rowsNotYetStored then reports no added answer, and foldPendingProgress retains only the stored row. The second answer and its ability contribution are lost.
findings.fix: Include category and compatible canonical provenance in legacy occurrence matching. Distinguish identity corrections of baseline rows from independent incoming occurrences; ambiguous matches must not consume an answer silently. Test colliding IDs with equal outcomes but different categories through foldPendingProgress.

findings.title: Concurrent new-card additions and undo overcount the daily allowance
findings.problem: mergeFcNew correctly unions added IDs and removes undone IDs, but then takes the maximum of the resulting count and both devices' previous counts. That maximum reintroduces a charge that the merged ID set has already refunded.
findings.failure_scenario: The shared baseline has ten introduced cards, including A. One device introduces K and reaches eleven; the other undoes A and reaches nine. Reconciliation produces ten IDs but count=11. newCardAllowance consequently permits only nine more cards instead of ten, and the incorrect charge persists across reloads.
findings.fix: Compute the count from the merged IDs plus explicitly tracked anonymous legacy charges, rather than taking the maximum of totals that include removed IDs. Add a concurrent add-versus-undo regression asserting that count remains consistent with the merged ledger.

assessment: Do not merge yet. The persistence reconciliation can resurrect erased history, discard distinct legacy answers, and incorrectly recompute streak protection. The concurrent new-card ledger also overcounts after an undo. Review was static; tests were not executed.
